inventory.notes: White masthead with a bin outline glyph and 'Dunmore District Council' in bold body text; pale green-grey ground. Eye goes 1) 'Book a slot' title, 2) the grid of white time tiles with amber 'Few left' chips, 3) the filled green Next. Day choice as four outlined buttons plus an 'Another day' link. Few-left slots are pulled into an unlabelled band above 'Morning'/'Afternoon', so the grid is not in time order. 'Opening days' white card at the bottom. One face (Avenir Next) in bold and regular; 4 px corners, borders, no shadows, no imagery. Copy: 'Choose a day and the 20-minute slot you will arrive in; the gate checks the reference and the vehicle.' No signature element. Primary action: Next, conventional and findable.

Back link, title, step line; segmented Car / Car with trailer / Van with a fourth square (i) button of equal weight; Permit number field with 'Starts DRC-, then five digits.'; seven bordered checkbox rows for waste; filled Next. At 1280 the column fills ~55% of the width, right side empty. Error state: red-bordered summary with linked errors and inline red messages; conventional and clear.

White 'Your booking' summary card with Change links, four text inputs, a line 'Nothing is paid. Bring the reference and something with your address on it.', filled 'Book this slot'. Dark theme is composed (lighter cards, mint button, salmon error border). Expired state shows a '–' in the Slot row next to 'Change slot'.

'Booked' title; card 'Your reference' with DR-204117 at ~32 px bold; card 'At the centre' with gate instructions; outlined 'Book another slot'. At 1440 the second card stops at about half width under a full-width first card, and an empty band sits below the footer. The reference is the most important object of the flow but gets only a modest size step.

swap.evidence: Swapped with (a) a library meeting-room booking and (b) a council bulky-waste collection request: masthead, pale ground, green filled button, outlined day buttons, bordered time tiles, summary card and checkbox rows all survive unchanged. Bound to this product: only copy (20-minute slots, DRC- permit, gate, Quarry Road, 'Rubble up to four bags'). With the name and copy hidden, nothing visual says recycling centre.

category_guess.evidence: Predicted default for a UK council transactional service: white masthead, one plain sans, a single civic green or blue accent, outlined options, step indicator, error summary box with links, bordered summary card. Every identity-carrying choice here matches that default (root/default/1280-light.png, vehicle/errors/375-light.png, confirm/default/1280-light.png). No element was chosen from the centre's own world (signage, bay numbers, waste-stream colours, the gate).

similar_prompt.evidence: Similar brief: 'book a swimming-lane session at a council leisure centre, phones, older users'. A capable generator would produce the same title + day buttons + time tile grid with Full/Few left tags + Next, the same green-on-pale palette and white cards. Overlap is near total; only the copy differs.

evidence: All three tests fail on the identity-carrying elements: masthead (bin glyph + name in bold body text), green-on-pale restrained palette, outlined day buttons, time-tile grid, white bordered cards.

Copy is genuinely product-bound (gate, DRC- permit, 20-minute slots, Quarry Road) and the structure is correctly conventional for Operate surfaces, but no visual element or signature belongs to this product.
The done page's reference DR-204117, the natural signature (the thing shown at the gate), is set as an ordinary card heading.

attributes.x_evidence: Council name in the masthead; plain public-service language ('Nothing is paid', 'call 01632 960771 on a weekday and we will free the slot'); conventional public-service form anatomy; no marketing, no promotional imagery.
One face, one green, borders not shadows, one filled button per step.
attributes.y_evidence: Pulls fully to bare: no mark beyond a stock glyph, no use of the centre's world, half-empty desktop layouts, the reference without emphasis, the dash placeholder in the expired state, a half-width card on done.

attributes.pair: firm about the rules, not stern
attributes.x_evidence: Rules stated beside their controls: 'Starts DRC-, then five digits.', 'Rubble is limited to four bags and mattresses to two.', 'Bring the reference and something with your address on it.'; error copy is direct ('Choose the vehicle you are bringing.').
attributes.y_evidence: Error summary heading 'There is a problem' is neutral rather than stern; nothing harsh.

mode_fit: All four surfaces are Operate/Read and correctly stay conventional and quiet: no motion, no hero moment, standard controls. The problem is not too much expression but none at all at the identity floor (masthead, reference).

detector_comparison.post_unseal_notes: Zero detector hits is consistent with my reading: the design avoids tells by containing almost nothing beyond defaults, which is exactly why it is generic and plain. No change to verdicts.

findings.title: Few-left slots pulled out of time order into an unlabelled band above Morning
findings.description: On the when step, every slot tagged 'Few left' is lifted out of the Morning/Afternoon groups and shown first in a band with no heading, so 08:20, 09:20 and 12:00-14:20 sit above 'Morning' while 08:00, 09:00 sit below it. The grid no longer reads as a day in order.
findings.impact: A resident who wants 'Saturday morning' around 09:20 and scans the Morning row may not find it there and may think it is gone or pick another slot.

evidence.detail: 08:20...14:20 Few left band above 'Morning' heading containing 08:00, 08:40, 09:00
ten Few-left tiles above Morning at 375; selected 09:20 sits in Morning, other 09:xx in the band

harm.statement: Residents booking a car for a particular part of the day scan Morning or Afternoon and may miss free 'Few left' slots placed out of order above, slowing the choice or leading to a worse slot.

findings.recommendation: Decide whether scarcity or time is the ordering; the brief's users think in times ('Saturday morning'), so keep slots in time order within their part of day and carry scarcity on the tile itself.

findings.title: Booking reference has no focal treatment on the done page
findings.description: DR-204117 is the one object the resident must show at the gate, yet it sits at about 32 px bold inside an ordinary white card, the same card style as the instructions below. Nothing composes it as the gate pass.
findings.impact: The natural signature of this product (the thing the attendant reads) is left as a default heading; the page has no focal point.
findings.recommendation: Decide how the reference, day, slot and vehicle should present as the thing read at the gate, so it becomes the done page's focal point and the product's signature.

findings.title: Identity is only the council name; 'plain, not bare' lands on bare
findings.description: Across all four surfaces the only identity is 'Dunmore District Council' in bold body text beside a stock bin outline glyph. No element comes from the centre's world (signage, waste streams, the gate, Quarry Road). DESIGN.md asks for 'plain, not bare'.
findings.impact: The flow reads as a default form; the declared attribute's Y side is what is shown.
findings.recommendation: Decide what identity floor the council's service carries on every step (a designed name, a colour role from the centre's own signage or waste streams) without adding a hero moment to Operate surfaces.

findings.title: Done page at wide widths: half-width card under a full-width card and an empty band below the footer
findings.description: At 1440 the 'At the centre' card ends at about 610 px while the reference card above spans 1088 px; below the footer an empty grey band fills the rest of the viewport.
findings.impact: Looks unfinished on desktop; columns stop short for no reason.
findings.recommendation: Decide one content width for the done page's cards and let the page ground run to the viewport bottom.

findings.title: Expired state shows a bare dash placeholder in the Slot row
findings.description: When the held slot has expired, the summary's Slot row reads '– · Change slot'.
findings.impact: A placeholder on show in a state residents meet after a delay; the row could say what happened.
findings.recommendation: Decide what the Slot row says when the hold has lapsed (the lost time, or a prompt to choose again).

findings.title: 'Few left' chip text appears lighter than the declared warning colour
findings.description: The amber 'Few left' text on its cream chip renders as a mid orange, visibly lighter than DESIGN.md's warning token #8a5a00, and at small bold size.
findings.impact: If below 4.5:1, older residents reading on phones may not read the availability tag.

harm.statement: Older residents choosing a slot on a phone may struggle to read the 'Few left' tag if its contrast is below the AA floor.
harm.requirement: PRODUCT.md, Accessibility needs: "WCAG 2.2 AA as the floor"

findings.recommendation: Measure the rendered chip contrast and bring it onto the declared warning role.

findings.title: Info (i) button styled as a fourth equal option in the vehicle segmented control
findings.description: The square (i) button sits in line with Car / Car with trailer / Van at the same height and border weight.
findings.impact: Blurs the boundary of the segmented choice; a small coherence lapse.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether the vehicle help belongs as a separated control or as the rule stated beside the choice, as DESIGN.md's 'rules beside the control' asks.

strengths: Rules stated beside the controls they govern, in plain gate-attendant voice (permit format, rubble and mattress limits, 'Nothing is paid').
Composed dark theme with lighter cards and mint actions, consistent with the use scene.
One filled button per step and a clear, linked error summary.
keep: Keep the gate-attendant copy and the one-filled-button-per-step discipline.
not_assessable: Motion, focus rings, hover and the info-open interaction cannot be judged from stills beyond their captured state.
notes: No baseline screenshots in the packet, so no pairwise comparison. Detector output had 0 hits. Bash cat of several files was denied once; files were read with the Read tool instead.
